params.body:
## What broke

After copying a vehicle (e.g. to turn a mistaken order form back into a listing, R S1-10.1), the photo tabs of the copy showed grey tiles. Clicking a tile opened the photo fine.

`OwnStockController::copyPhotos` copies the original, cut-out and thumbnail files into the copy's folder and rewrites the row's paths, but kept `media_version` and `media_set` from the original. `VehicleImageService::url` treats those as "derived sizes exist for this path" and points md, sm and thumb at `_afgeleid/{copy path}/{version}-{size}`, which nobody ever wrote. The lightbox asks for the plain file, which does exist. A photo whose cut-out was not in the bucket kept pointing at the original's cut-out (whose sizes exist), which is why one tile out of seventeen did show.

## The fix

A copied row whose shown file (cut-out if any, else original, as `url()` picks it) moves to the copy's folder gets `media_version` and `media_set` null, like a fresh upload and like the bought-over copy already does (R S5-3.17). The URL falls back to the plain file at once and the five-minute sweep (`stocklist:fotos-afgeleid`) writes the copy's own sizes. A row that still shows the original's file keeps its version.

- New rule R S1-10.4, finding `2026-10-06-een-gekopieerde-wagen-toonde-lege-fototegels`.
- `ACopiedVehicleGetsItsOwnPhotoSizesTest`: fails on main, passes here.
- Full suite green locally (2996 tests), PHPStan clean, Pint on the new file.

## After deploy

Copies made before this have rows that still claim the original's sizes. Repair one car (dry run first):

```
php artisan stocklist:fotos-afgeleid --missing --wagen=<id>
php artisan stocklist:fotos-afgeleid --missing --wagen=<id> --apply
```

The Fiat 500 copy reported today is most likely vehicle 23312 (from the screenshot's status bar; check the id on its sheet). `--missing` without `--wagen` counts every affected photo across all copies.
params.title: A copied vehicle shows its photos instead of grey tiles
